about.title: About SustainableCrafting
about.missionDescription: At SustainableCrafting, we provide a digital platform to enable artisans worldwide to document their handmade products, connect, and support their socioeconomic activities. We believe in preserving the knowledge, skills, and cultural heritage embedded in every by-hand tradition. Our mission is to champion authenticity, celebrate the human story behind every handmade object, and promote sustainability in a global marketplace that too often forgets the skilled artisan hands that create them.
about.keyFeatures: The database includes a Prisma wired to Postgres via env-driven URLs for dev and Docker. UI includes the shadcn/ui with Tailwind v3, radix primitives, and reusable utilities. All packaged in a Docker container for easy deployment.

footer.description: The project website has been produced and is managed by the University of Brighton. This project is funded by the UK's Arts and Humanities Research Council under the India-UK research into creative industries and cultural heritage with the title: Crafting a Sustainable Future: Empowering Indian Crafts in the Creative Industries. (Grant No. OPP080).

landing.description: Connect directly with skilled artisans from across the world. Every skillfully designed product tells an authentic story about the place, its histories, and the people who create them. Verify their authenticity through our innovative QR code system.

connected.title: Connected
connected.description: Direct link to artisans and makers

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.subtitle: Every craft on this site carries the story of the person who made it, and a signature that lets anyone check where it came from.

visitors.heading: If you are here to look
visitors.lead: You may have arrived by scanning a code on a piece of work, or simply by browsing. Either way, here is what you can find out.

steps.title: Meet the maker
steps.body: Every craft is linked to the artisan who made it. Their profile carries their story in their own words, often in their own voice, with the workshop and tools behind the work.

steps.title: Watch the story
steps.body: Many artisans record a short film about their craft: where they learned it, what it means to them, and how a piece is made. English captions are generated automatically, whatever language they speak.

steps.title: Check the credential
steps.body: Photographs and videos are signed with content credentials as they are uploaded, and each documented craft is issued a verifiable credential. Together these record what was created here and by which account.

steps.title: Verify it yourself
steps.body: You do not have to take our word for it. Paste a credential into the verification page and check the signature independently. It will tell you whether the file has been altered since it was signed.

artisans.heading: If you make things
artisans.lead: The site is built for artisans to document their own work, in their own language, without needing to be a photographer or a writer.

steps.title: Create your profile
steps.body: Tell people who you are, where you work, and how you learned your craft. You choose what to share, including whether to show the area you work in.

steps.title: Record your story
steps.body: Answer six questions by speaking or writing, whichever is easier. Add photographs and video of your workshop, tools and process, and we assemble them into a short film. If you already have a film of your own, upload it instead.

steps.title: Document your crafts
steps.body: Add each piece with its materials, technique and measurements. Every craft receives a credential automatically, so its origin travels with it.

steps.title: Put your code on your work
steps.body: Your profile has its own QR code. Print it, attach it to a label or a card, and anyone who scans it lands on your story rather than on a marketplace listing.

tradition.title: Bridging Tradition with Technology
tradition.description: Our QR code system creates an unbreakable link between handmade crafts and their creators. Each scan reveals the artisan's story, the materials used, and the traditional techniques that make every piece unique and valuable.

intro.title: Guideline for Sharing Your Craft Story
intro.lead: This page will help you tell the story of your craft in your own words. These questions are only here to guide you. Please speak naturally and add anything you feel is important.
intro.formatsTitle: You can share your story as:
intro.encouragement: Please answer in your own words, like you are telling your story to someone who wants to understand your craft.
intro.alreadyHaveFilmTitle: Already have a film of your own?
intro.alreadyHaveFilmBody: Upload it and it becomes your story film. You can still add a short summary afterwards, and we will add English captions.

step1.title: About Yourself
step1.prompt: Can you tell us who you are and how you first learned this craft?

step2.title: About Your Craft
step2.prompt: Can you explain your craft in simple words, including where it comes from, how it is made, and what it is used for?

step3.title: Feelings, Meaning, and Connections
step3.prompt: What does this craft mean to you? Are there any feelings, events, traditions, symbols, or stories connected to it?

step4.title: Benefits and Opportunities
step4.prompt: What has this craft brought to you, your family, or your community?

step5.title: Challenges and Barriers
step5.prompt: What difficulties do you face in practicing this craft, and what kind of support would help keep it alive?

step6.title: Knowledge Transfer and Future Generations
step6.prompt: How is this craft passed on to younger people, and do you think it can continue in the future?

step7.title: Products, Tools and Processes
step7.prompt: Upload photos or videos of your workshop, tools, materials, products, and making process. Please choose images that are related to the story you are telling. If you upload more than one, please arrange them in the order you want people to see them.
step7.saveFirst: Save an answer in a previous step first, then come back to add workshop media.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal information Sustainable Crafting collects, why we collect it, and what rights you have over it. It applies to this website and to the accounts, artisan profiles, craft records and story films created through it.

sections.heading: Who we are
sections.body:
Sustainable Crafting is a research project website produced and managed by the University of Brighton. The project is funded by the UK’s Arts and Humanities Research Council under the India-UK research into creative industries and cultural heritage, grant number OPP080.

For the purposes of UK data protection law, the University of Brighton is the data controller for personal information processed through this website.

sections.heading: How to contact us
sections.body: If you have a question about this policy, or you want to exercise any of the rights described below, write to us at privacy@PLACEHOLDER.invalid.

sections.heading: The information we collect
sections.body:
Account information. When you create an account we store your name, your email address and a hash of your password. If you sign in with Google we store the account identifier, name, email address and profile image that Google provides. We never receive or store your Google password.

Artisan profile. If you create an artisan profile we store the first and last name, country and region you enter, together with anything else you choose to add: a biography, years of experience, how you learned your craft, a website, social media handles and hashtags. You may also record the approximate latitude and longitude of where you work.

Craft records. Titles, descriptions, materials, techniques, measurements, photographs and videos of the pieces you document, and optionally the place where a piece was made.

My Story. Your written answers to the story questions, the audio and video you record or upload, photographs and videos of your workshop, tools, materials and process, and the short summary that introduces your story. From this material we generate English captions, a transcript and an assembled story film.

Communities. Your membership of any community on the site, and the role you hold in it.

Technical information. A session cookie that keeps you signed in, a cookie that remembers your language choice, and ordinary server logs recording requests made to the site.

sections.heading: Recordings and sensitive information
sections.body:
Story recordings carry your face and your voice, and they often describe your family, your community, your traditions and your beliefs. Depending on what you choose to say, a recording may reveal information that data protection law treats as a special category, such as ethnic origin or religious belief.

We process this material only because you have chosen to provide it and have consented to it being published. You can withdraw that consent at any time by unpublishing your story or by asking us to delete it.

sections.heading: Why we process your information
sections.body:
To provide your account and the service you asked for, we process your account and profile information because it is necessary to perform our agreement with you.

To publish your craft records, your story and your film, we rely on your consent, which you give when you choose to publish. Published material is visible to anyone who visits the site.

To generate captions, transcripts and draft summaries from your recordings, we rely on your consent, which you give when you choose to record or upload.

To keep the site secure and working, including rate limiting and error logging, we rely on our legitimate interest in operating a safe service.

As a research project we may report anonymous or aggregated statistics about how the site is used. That material does not identify you.

sections.heading: Who we share it with
sections.body:
We do not sell your personal information and we do not use it for advertising.

Automated transcription. Audio and video from your story recordings is sent to Groq, a service provider in the United States, which produces the English captions and transcripts and drafts summary text. Only the media needed for that task is sent.

Sign in with Google. If you choose this option, Google processes the sign in under its own privacy policy.

Maps and embedded video. Craft pages can show a map from OpenStreetMap and video embedded from YouTube. Neither loads until you choose to open it. When you do, that provider receives your IP address and may set its own cookies. Some pages also display images hosted by Wikimedia.

Hosting. The site, its database and its media storage are operated for the project rather than on a public cloud bucket.

sections.heading: Information leaving the UK
sections.body: Groq processes recordings in the United States. Where personal information leaves the UK we rely on the safeguards required by UK data protection law, including the International Data Transfer Agreement or Addendum where these apply.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
sections.body:
Account and profile information is kept for as long as your account is open. Deleting your artisan profile deletes the crafts and the story attached to it. Deleting a media file removes both the database record and the stored file.

Unpublished drafts stay in your account until you delete them. Server logs are kept only for as long as they are needed to operate and secure the site.

sections.heading: Access to what you upload
sections.body:
Published material is public by design and can be seen by anyone visiting the site.

Material you have not published is not listed anywhere public and is not linked from any page. Media files are served from an address containing a long random identifier, and anyone holding that address can open the file. Please treat an unpublished upload as unlisted rather than as private, and do not upload anything you would not want seen if its address were shared.

sections.heading: Security
sections.body:
Passwords are stored only as hashes and never in a readable form. The keys held in the credential vault are encrypted before they are stored. Content credentials are signed with certificates issued for your artisan identity, so a file can be checked for alteration after signing.

No website can promise perfect security. If a breach affects your rights we will tell you and the Information Commissioner’s Office as the law requires.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body:
Under UK data protection law you can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold about you, ask us to correct information that is wrong, ask us to delete information, ask us to restrict or stop using it, and ask to receive certain information in a portable form. Where we rely on your consent, you can withdraw it at any time.

To exercise any of these rights, write to privacy@PLACEHOLDER.invalid. If you are unhappy with our response you can complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office at ico.org.uk.

sections.heading: Cookies
sections.body:
This site sets only the cookies it needs in order to work. There are no analytics cookies, no advertising cookies and no third party tracking on the site.

A session cookie is set when you sign in. It identifies your session so that you stay signed in, and it is cleared when you sign out.

A language cookie records the language you selected, so the site appears in that language when you return.

Because both are strictly necessary for functions you have asked for, we do not ask for consent before setting them. You can clear cookies in your browser at any time, though the site cannot keep you signed in without the session cookie.

sections.heading: Children
sections.body: This site is intended for adults. If you are under 18, please use it only with the involvement of a parent or guardian.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
sections.body: If we change this policy we will update the date shown at the top of this page. Where a change materially affects how we use your information, we will bring it to your attention when you next sign in.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of Sustainable Crafting. By creating an account or using the site, you agree to them.

sections.heading: About this service
sections.body: Sustainable Crafting is a research project website produced and managed by the University of Brighton, funded by the UK’s Arts and Humanities Research Council under grant OPP080. It gives artisans a place to document their craft, record their story, and publish both with content credentials that record how the material was made.

sections.heading: Your account
sections.body:
You must provide accurate registration details and keep your password confidential. You are responsible for what happens through your account, so tell us promptly if you think someone else has gained access to it.

You must be 18 or over to create an account, or have the involvement of a parent or guardian.

sections.heading: Your content stays yours
sections.body:
You keep ownership of everything you upload: your photographs, your videos, your recordings, your written answers and your craft records.

By publishing material on the site you grant the University of Brighton a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty free licence to store, reproduce, translate, adapt for captions and subtitles, and display that material, for the purpose of operating and presenting this website and describing the research project. This licence exists so that we can host your work, generate captions and assemble your story film. It ends for future use when you unpublish or delete the material, although we cannot recall copies that other people have already taken.

You confirm that you have the right to publish what you upload, that it is your own work or that you have permission to use it, and that anyone identifiable in a photograph or a recording has agreed to appear.

sections.heading: Publishing and consent
sections.body: Material stays unpublished until you choose to publish it. When you publish a story, that story and its film become visible to anyone who visits the site, including your name, your recordings and any location you chose to share. You can unpublish at any time.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
sections.body:
Do not use this site to publish material that is unlawful, that misleads people about the origin of a craft, that is abusive, or that infringes anyone else’s rights. Do not try to gain unauthorised access to the site, to other accounts or to the systems behind it. Do not use automated means to extract material from the site at scale.

We may remove material or suspend an account that breaches these terms.

sections.heading: Content credentials
sections.body:
The site signs media with C2PA content credentials and issues verifiable credentials for craft records. These record what was created on this site and by which account, and they let anyone check that a file has not been altered since it was signed.

They are not an independent verification that your description is true. We do not inspect or certify claims about materials, technique, origin or age.

sections.heading: Availability
sections.body: This is a research project and the site is provided as it is. We cannot promise uninterrupted availability, and features may change or be withdrawn as the research continues. Please keep your own copies of anything that matters to you.

sections.heading: Liability

Nothing in these terms limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for anything else that cannot lawfully be limited.

Subject to that, the University of Brighton is not liable for indirect or consequential loss, for loss of profit or opportunity, or for the loss of material of which you did not keep your own copy.

sections.heading: Ending your use of the site
sections.body: You can stop using the site and delete your account at any time. Deleting your artisan profile deletes the crafts and the story attached to it. We may suspend or end access where these terms are breached.

sections.body: We may update these terms as the project develops. The date at the top of this page shows when they last changed. Continuing to use the site after a change means you accept the updated terms.
